The department will construct the cul-de-sac on Sunnyside Avenue as part of the Lincoln Highway Improvement and will remove the existing Sunnyside Avenue pavement. Included will be the grading and sodding of this area.
By closing this portion of Sunnyside Street, the present playground area to the west will become immediately contiguous to the school building, thus eliminating the hazard inherent in school children crossing the street to use this facility.
No significant changes in physical effects on the school land users is expected because none of the land to be acquired from the school will be used for highway purposes. Instead the land will be used to replace parkways, sidewalks and a pedestrian underpass.
The Regional Wastewater Plan, adopted by the Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission on March 3, 1971, is the first in a series of plans dealing with the management of the water resources in northeastern Illinois. Other plans in this series include water supply and flood control. Taken together, they comprise the Regional Water Resource Management Plan, an implementing element of the Comprehensive General Plan which sets forth overall development goals and policies for the six county area.
A closed drainage system will be built along the entire improvement. All drainage will be directed into the existing drainage courses. Drainage for the Lincoln Highway Improvement will be in accordance with the provisions and limitations established by the General Assembly of the State of Illinois, and contained in the Illinois Revised Statutes.
Based upon the enactment of this legislation, the use of highway funds for other than highway purposes is restricted. Highway drainage is designed to prevent the accumulation and retention of water on and by the highway.
